_comment: SH978/SH980 — every surface this console offers, how an agent reaches the same capability, and
the words used when it cannot.
The backend owns this file because the readers are on both sides: ShConsoleSurfaceP1Test joins
it to the manifest, the MCP tool list and the batch ops; the console builds its rail from it;
`shio://surfaces` and `shio surfaces` publish it. Icons, titles and i18n keys stay in
bento-nav.ts, where they must live — this is the half a JVM has to be able to read.
A surface names an `agent` equivalent — a tool, an op or a declared endpoint, each resolved
against the running server — or an `exception` whose `reason` is one of the words in `reasons`
below. `consoleOnly` is the same vocabulary applied to what is console-only by nature: a later
task adds one classified entry there instead of arguing its P1 position in prose nothing reads.
`deepLinks` is how the backend answers `where is this in the console` (SH981): a template per
kind of thing an agent writes, substituted with the id it already holds. Declared here because
the console's prefix has moved once already — a URL concatenated in Java would have rotted
silently, and bento-nav.test.mjs holds each template against the router's own routes.

operator-only.means: a person's own credential is the point: an agent doing this would be an escalation rather than a convenience
operator-only.falsifier: an agent op or endpoint appearing for it, which would mean the boundary moved and nobody said so

navigation.means: a way of getting somewhere rather than a capability — a hub, a landing page
navigation.falsifier: the surface gaining a capability of its own, at which point it needs an answer like any other

rest-only.means: a delivery surface a front end queries, which the manifest points at rather than carrying
rest-only.falsifier: the capability arriving on the agent surface, which makes the pointer the wrong answer

gap.means: no agent form, nothing declares it, and the task that closes it is named

chrome.means: how the console renders itself — a shell, a provider, a layout. An agent reads content, not chrome
chrome.falsifier: an agent surface growing a rendering concern, which would mean this is not chrome after all

accessibility.means: how a person operates the console with a keyboard or a screen reader
accessibility.falsifier: the same affordance being asked for by a client that is not a browser

cache.means: how the console holds what it already fetched. An agent fetches what it needs when it needs it
cache.falsifier: a caching contract appearing on the agent surface, which would make this shared rather than the console's

preference.means: what a person chooses about their own view, stored for them
preference.falsifier: the preference changing what the instance does rather than what one person sees

contract-leg.means: the console's half of a contract whose other halves exist — it is the human end, so there is nothing for an agent to call
contract-leg.falsifier: the other legs disappearing, which would leave this console-only in fact rather than by design

surfaces.capability: browse a site's folders and posts
find content across a site
read and change the content model
the media library
list what was deleted, and put it back
read what arrived through a site's form, and where it lands
see what goes live or comes down, and when
edit a page where it is rendered
the administration hub

exception.why: a landing page listing the surfaces below it, which is a way of getting somewhere rather than a capability. The manifest is what an agent reads to find its way, and it has no counterpart to a hub

surfaces.capability: who may sign in, their groups and what each role permits

exception.why: an agent that could add a user or widen a role could grant itself a human's access, which is the escalation minting its own token would be

surfaces.capability: mint and revoke API tokens

exception.why: an agent minting or widening its own credential is the escalation Block L exists to prevent — the one boundary here that must never move

surfaces.capability: the SH22 tenant catalogue

exception.why: a tenant is the isolation boundary the agent's own scoping is derived from, so writing one is the operator's act

surfaces.capability: how humans log in

exception.why: an operator decision about identity, and an agent that could rewrite it could let itself in as somebody else

surfaces.capability: where an exchange package may come from

exception.why: instance wiring rather than content: it says which stranger's package this installation will accept

surfaces.capability: SMTP credentials

exception.why: an agent writing these could redirect the instance's mail

surfaces.capability: tell a front end that content changed
browse and install blueprint packages
what happened to this page, and to this site

exception.why: /agent/changes walks the same audit rows by cursor and cannot answer 'what happened to this page', which is the question a correction starts from (SH973 found the same hole from the controller side)

surfaces.capability: approve or revert an agent's run

exception.why: the human's veto over the agent's work (SH109). Reachable with an operator's own credential over HTTP, which is what SH975's OPERATOR_HTTP records, and refused to an AGENT token

surfaces.capability: query delivery content as a front end does

exception.why: the delivery surface a front end queries (Block A), which the manifest points at with POST /graphql. An agent reads content through /agent/read instead

consoleOnly.why: one section provider above the router, so every page renders in the same shell (SH958). Nothing an agent reads passes through it
the audit log keeps a readable column rather than becoming a mosaic (SH906). The same rows reach an agent through the change feed, unlaid-out
the Universal Editor's in-browser bridge (SH907). Its other leg is /agent/editable, which answers the same question without a DOM — this half is the human end of that contract
how the console holds what it fetched between navigations. An agent's read is a call it decided to make, and a cache between them would be a staleness it did not ask for
a failed render becomes a message inside the shell rather than a blank page. An agent's failures are teaching 4xx and incidents, which is the same job answered where its caller is
every field in the post editor is reachable and announced by its label. An agent writes fields by name and never meets a label
a keyboard reaches the page's content without walking the rail first
what a curator lets the dock report, and how loudly (SH971). The agent's own outcomes are on the change feed whatever a person chose to be shown
a curator's names for filtered lists, which are URLs (SH1024). An agent states its query every time on shio_find, and the words a view saves are those same words
